title: 1. Start with the stakeholder’s site
detail: The first page has no preloaded township, invented workers or rain. Choose the site files first.

title: 2. Upload the source file
detail: This fictional bundle supplies surveyed-style geometry, drainage tables and rainfall. Its provenance stays synthetic.

title: 3. Review what can be used
detail: 5 nodes, 4 pipes, 49 terrain points, 3 roads and 8 buildings. Input completeness is separate from field validation.

title: 4. Build the matching 3D site
detail: Terrain, roads, footprints and pipe connections come from this file. The sequence reveals imported layers.

title: 5. Inspect an uploaded asset
detail: MH-C uses the uploaded ID, position and elevations. No fixed D07 dataset is required.

title: 6. Review the model assumptions
detail: Native SWMM models this 1D network. Soil defaults and direct catchment entry are disclosed before calculation.

title: 7. Calculate the uploaded baseline
detail: About 1,597 m³ leaves drainage nodes over the run. This is calculated by EPA SWMM, not a dashboard lookup.

title: 8. Test one physical change
detail: The uploaded LINK-TRUNK pipe changes from 0.30 m to 0.60 m. Same rainfall and site; loss is about 149 m³.

title: 9. Explain the result honestly
detail: Node columns and this curve show depth above the pipe invert. Street flood depth and flooded houses are not inferred.

title: 10. Save a reviewable action
detail: The Draft links actual run IDs and original source hashes. Cost remains unknown. Engineering review comes before expenditure.

title: 11. Track the real operating question
detail: The register links the complaint to LINK-TRUNK and assigns investigation follow-up. Practice reports remain synthetic.

title: 12. Retain the evidence chain
detail: Source text, SHA-256, model version and synthetic inspection stay visible. Visual coverage does not secretly change pipe hydraulics.

title: 13. Resume the saved project
detail: The API retains the imported model and native runs. Problem follow-up remains scoped to this browser and project.

title: 14. Show what happens when data is missing
detail: This second file lacks MH-C invert, LINK-TRUNK diameter, catchments and rainfall. It can map, but cannot simulate.

title: 15. A specific next data-collection task
detail: The manager knows exactly what measurements are missing. The app does not invent the values or replace a failed calculation with mock output.
